verdicts.originalText:
Dreamdrifter (skill) state in-game disables Normal and Charged Attacks — only Q, swap, dash, and re-pressing E (which exits the state) are allowed. The schema doesn't gate invalid actions, so typing N or C during the 5s stance window will produce a normal/charge block on the timeline that wouldn't fire in-game. User assumes responsibility for valid sequencing.

A1 swirl extension: stance window can extend by +2.5s per swirl event (max 2× = +5s). The planner's cast-only reaction emission (E3 v1.5) fires one swirl per E/Q cast on Mizuki, so a typical `Mizuki E ... Q` rotation extends the stance by +5s (the in-game maximum). Per-N anemo hits and drift-cloud ticks are not modeled, so swirl-heavy rotations under-fire compared to gcsim — accepted approximation.
verdicts.proposedText: In game the stance blocks Normal and Charged Attacks; typing N or C still shows a block on the timeline, so sequence valid actions yourself. Swirls extend it up to +5s, but only one is counted per skill or burst cast, so some rotations show a shorter stance.
verdicts.rationale: Two real divergences buried in curator-grade detail plus banned tokens ('schema', 'gcsim', 'E3 v1.5', backtick notation) and the character's own name. Part A — the stance blocks Normal/Charged in game but the tool doesn't prevent them — is an unwired limitation (no action-gating capability on the CAN list), so rewrite, not implementDelete. Part B — the swirl duration extension IS modeled (durationExtensions on onReaction) but cast-only, so certain rotations under-extend — is a legitimate approximation caveat. Compressed to the two outcomes a timeline reader needs; numeric breakdown, allowed-action list, and the per-N/drift-cloud cause demoted.

Extension is +2.5s per swirl event, max 2 (net +5s)
A typical E...Q rotation reaches the +5s in-game maximum; pure-E or zero-Q rotations under-fire by 50%

demotedNotes: In-game the Dreamdrifter stance blocks Normal/Charged; only Q, swap, dash, and re-press-E (which exits) are valid inputs. Base stance window is 5s. The tool does not gate invalid actions, so N/C typed during the window render as blocks that wouldn't fire in game.

A1 extension: +2.5s per swirl, max 2 (=+5s). Cast-only reaction emission fires one swirl per anemo E/Q cast, so a typical E...Q reaches the +5s in-game max while pure-E or zero-Q rotations under-fire by ~50%; per-N anemo hits and drift-cloud ticks aren't counted (accepted approximation).

verdicts.originalText: Mini Baku's tick markers represent snack spawn events (every 1.5s). Each snack resolves to EITHER a heal or a Munen Shockwave explosion, not both: picked up by a party member below 70% HP it heals them (235% of Mizuki's Elemental Mastery + 692 at Talent Lvl 10); picked up above 70% HP — or left uncollected for 4s — it explodes for 127% ATK Anemo. The planner shows both a heal marker and a damage marker on every tick to represent the two possible outcomes, but in a real fight each snack becomes only one of them, so neither the total healing nor the total damage is additive across all ticks. When Mizuki herself picks up a snack the heal is doubled (+100%); the planner shows the base, non-doubled amount. Pickup and explosion can also lag the rendered spawn tick by up to 4s.
verdicts.proposedText: Each tick shows both a heal and a damage marker, but a snack resolves to only one — heal or explosion — so the markers aren't additive across ticks. Self-pickup doubles the heal, though the base amount is shown; pickup or explosion can also lag the marked tick by up to 4s.
verdicts.rationale: The core divergence — the heal and damage markers on each tick are two possible outcomes of one snack, not both, so they must not be summed — is decision-relevant and has to survive, so rewrite over delete. Never implementDelete: the 70% HP routing is recipientHpBelow (optimistic-by-design, legitimately caveated) and the snack-pickup mechanic is pickup-driven empowerment, out of scope by constitution. Compressed to mutual-exclusivity, the self-double heal shown at base, and the up-to-4s timing lag; heal/damage formulas and the explicit 70% threshold demoted (damage math + kit knowledge). Dropped the character name and 'Mini Baku'/'Munen Shockwave' proper nouns as unnecessary.
